headline: 5 Myths About Juvenile Cases That Could Harm Your Child

publisher.name: Law Office of Angelo J. Reyes, APC

articleBody:
When your child is facing legal trouble, there's a lot of misinformation out there. Let's clear up some common myths:

Myth: Juvenile records are automatically sealed and won't follow my child into adulthood.
Fact: Not all juvenile records are automatically sealed or expunged. Many stay on file unless specific action is taken to clear them, and they can impact future opportunities like college applications, employment, or military service. It's crucial to explore record-clearing options with an attorney.

Myth: Juvenile cases are less serious than adult cases, so legal representation isn't as critical.
Fact: While the juvenile system focuses on rehabilitation, the consequences can still be severe, including detention, strict probation terms, and a lasting record. Having an experienced defense attorney is just as vital as in an adult case to protect your child's rights and future.

Myth: My child doesn't need an attorney if they admit guilt; it will make things easier.
Fact: Admitting guilt without legal counsel can be a huge mistake. Your child might not fully understand their rights or the potential consequences. An attorney can assess the evidence, negotiate with prosecutors, and ensure any admissions are made with full awareness of the legal implications.

Myth: Parents can easily represent their child in juvenile court.
Fact: The juvenile justice system is complex, with specific rules, procedures, and legal terminology. A parent, even with the best intentions, isn't equipped to provide the same level of defense as a seasoned juvenile defense attorney who understands the nuances of the system.

Myth: If my child is a minor, they can't be charged as an adult.
Fact: In certain serious cases or depending on the child's age and criminal history, minors can indeed be tried as adults. This is a very serious outcome with significant adult consequences, making skilled legal defense absolutely essential to fight such a transfer.
